candidate.title: TAIL-seq
candidate.scope: The single TAIL-seq row of the supplied Illumina poster: preparation of an adaptor-flanked cDNA library from rRNA-depleted RNA to represent native mRNA 3′ termini and poly(A) tails. The row has no alternative branch. Adjacent TATL-seq, RARseq and PAL-seq rows and the chemical legend are context, not targets. The matching catalogue page and checked review passages clarify the depicted route; reported readout properties describe the cDNA endpoint without adding unshown sequencing or analysis operations. This is a schematic architecture, not an execution protocol.

features: Input is already depleted of ribosomal RNA; depletion is preparation history, not a separately drawn operation.
Depicted target is an RNA body continuous with a native 3′ poly(A) tail, labeled AAAA(A)n; the target property is tail length.

states.label: Purified, amplified adaptor-flanked cDNA library
features: Final product is labeled cDNA; its insert represents retained native RNA terminal sequence, including poly(A), between adaptor-derived ends.
Library molecules preserve the within-fragment association between transcript-derived sequence and that RNA molecule’s 3′ tail.
Reported paired-end readout assigns transcript identity from the fragment’s body-side read and estimates poly(A) length from its tail-side read; terminal modifications are also a TAIL-seq readout.
Homopolymer fluorescence carryover can overestimate tail length; the review reports fluorescence re-analysis as part of TAIL-seq interpretation. It is not drawn as another library-preparation step.

operations.label: 3′ adaptor ligation
operations.description: Append a biotinylated 3′ adaptor to the RNA’s existing terminal end. The output retains the native tail and gains an adaptor and affinity handle.
operations.mechanism: RNA 3′-end adaptor ligation; the enzyme is not named in the supplied schematic.
operations.information_effect: Places a capture/sequencing interface beyond the native tail, preserving terminal sequence rather than selecting by oligo(dT) binding.

operations.label: Partial digestion with RNase T1
operations.description: Partially cleave the transcript body, producing shorter RNA fragments while leaving a 3′-adaptor-bearing terminal fragment with the depicted poly(A) tract.
operations.mechanism: The full-text review states that RNase T1 cleaves downstream of guanosine; the homopolymeric A tract is protected from this cleavage.
operations.information_effect: Removes upstream transcript continuity while retaining nearby transcript sequence physically linked to the native tail and 3′ adaptor.

operations.label: Pull down with streptavidin
operations.description: Capture biotinylated, 3′-adaptor-bearing RNA fragments on streptavidin; the output differs by affinity enrichment and attachment to the drawn support.
operations.mechanism: Biotin on the 3′ adaptor binds the streptavidin capture component.
operations.information_effect: Selects fragments carrying the original adaptor-tagged 3′ end, rather than retaining every upstream RNase T1 fragment. This chemical selection alone does not prove that every retained RNA is mRNA.

operations.label: 5′ end phosphorylation
operations.description: Phosphorylate the retained RNA fragments’ 5′ ends after capture, creating the ligatable 5′-phosphate boundary before gel purification. Release from the capture support is not attributed to this reaction.
operations.mechanism: Addition of a 5′ phosphate; the schematic does not name an enzyme or show an end-group structure.
operations.information_effect: Changes the ligation interface while retaining the transcript-tail-adaptor association.

operations.description: Purify and size-select the phosphorylated terminal RNA fragments. The output is the selected adaptor-bearing terminal RNA population drawn without a capture support.

The candidate catalogue page is headed TAIL-Seq: Poly(A) Tail Sequencing and repeats this route; Chang et al. is identified as the method paper. The abstract supports target/readout, while the matching figure, catalogue and full-text review support local preparation architecture. None of the adjacent poster methods or cited applications is an alternative target.
